correctness.rationale: The full reachable family is exactly the preimage under the Bloch Hopf projection of the spherical cap beta<=min(2m theta,pi): the triangle inequality proves necessity, half-turns and connected phase parameter space prove sufficiency, and the rightmost phase gate supplies the complete Hopf fiber. Maximizing trace process fidelity over this cap is equivalent to minimizing great-circle distance of Bloch rays, yielding cos^2((beta-c)_+/2); a Haar-uniform Bloch polar density sin(beta)/2 integrates to the stated complete distribution and explicit mean. The quartic coefficient 1/96 follows from an exact Taylor series; boundaries theta=pi/2,m=0,m large and pole targets are covered. Ninety numerical assertions passed in verify.py; they are checks rather than substitutes for analytic quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Eligible October 13, 2026 paper concerns universal word length and average over random basis pairs; Hamada 2014 proves exact two-axis factor counts and cap reachability, both explicitly credited. The evaluated new statement is a sharp best-approximation process-fidelity functional at a fixed insufficient number of tilted pulses and its full Haar-target law and quartic mean-versus-quadratic worst-case threshold. Full-text direct comparisons and six published-finding corpus semantic searches identified no claim that directly asserts or dominates that combined functional. Priority remains best knowledge, with a residual risk of unlocated geometric consequences.

value.rationale: A fixed number of costly tilted-axis segments with freely applied phase rotations is a natural constrained single-qubit compilation architecture. The entire best-achievable target process-fidelity functional and its Haar distribution give quantitative approximation benchmarks below the known exact-generation threshold. The exact quartic average infidelity versus quadratic worst-case infidelity near that threshold is a nontrivial sharp operational distinction, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a relabeling of exact word-count bounds.
